blocks.html: Although the law presumes of men that each one is good, of good life and of honest conversation [manner of living] a, and that none of them has the intention to do wrong b: nevertheless, in one who has once been wicked and caught in some wickedness, the law with great reason thinks and presumes him to be always such, in the same kind of wickedness c. As for example one who has at some time stolen, if he is again accused of theft, upon however small a proof from other conjecture there may be, one will easily presume him to be a thief today. And she who has once fornicated, that she still goes astray; and he who in the first accusation has been a calumniator, that he is so again in the second d. Of which and the like the reason is not hard to understand: for it is likely that in a will declared by deed or by word each one continues and perseveres e; inasmuch as a change of accident or quality (which consists in fact) is not easily presumed f. Rather, one draws argument and conjecture from the past to the present time and to the future g: as one whom one has once known to be rich, one presumes him still today rich; or poor, still poor; one who has been lord of a place, to be so afterwards; a subject, to be so still; and so of the like h.

notes.citation: Digest 31.77.25 (De legatis II, l. Cum pater, § Rogo; Papinian: Rogo, filia, bona tua quandoque distribuas liberis tuis… — the children are presumed to have deserved unless they have offended), not D. 31.88 as formerly suggested; Decretals X 2.23.16 (De praesumptionibus, c. Dudum: one provided "if he be fit" need not prove his fitness, quum idoneus praesumatur)
notes.original: l. cũ Pater. P rogo. D. de leg. ij. dudum. de præſ.
notes.gloss: The canonists' rule that everyone is presumed good until the contrary is proved.

notes.citation: Liber Sextus, De regulis iuris, reg. 8: Semel malus semper praesumitur esse malus
notes.original: c. ſemel malus, au vi. de reg. iur.
notes.gloss: Once bad, always presumed bad — the rule Coras's whole annotation turns on.

notes.citation: Digest 48.2.7 (De accusationibus et inscriptionibus, l. Si cui; Ulpian), § Eiusdem (paragraph not identified); Decretals X 2.23.9 (De praesumptionibus, c. Scribam); Decretum, C. 22 q. 5 c. 14, Parvuli (children not to be compelled to swear; the perjurer not to be a witness afterwards)
notes.original: l. ſi cui. P. eiuſdem. D. de accuſatio. c. ſcribã. de p̃teſump. c. paruuli. xxij. q. v.
notes.gloss: Presumptions against the previously convicted; the print's p̃te ſump. is præſump.

notes.citation: Digest 35.1.89 (De condicionibus et demonstrationibus, l. Non ad ea)
notes.original: l. nõ ad ea, D. de cond. & . demonſt.
notes.gloss: The print sets the point tight after the ampersand.

notes.citation: Digest 22.3.22 (De probationibus et praesumptionibus, l. Eum qui)
notes.original: l. eum qui D. de Proba
notes.gloss: A change of state is not presumed but must be proved by him who alleges it.

notes.citation: Digest 20.6.8.7 (Quibus modis pignus vel hypotheca solvitur, l. Sicut, § Supervacuum; Marcian); Code 4.19.16 (De probationibus, l. Sive possidetis; Diocletian and Maximian)
notes.original: l. ſicut P. ſuperuacuũ. D. qui mo. pig. ſol. l. ſiue poſtidens. C. de proba.
notes.gloss: Argument from the past to the present: a state once shown to exist is presumed to continue; the print's poſtidens is a wrong sort for poſſidens (the law Sive possidetis).

notes.citation: Code 4.19.3 (De probationibus, l. Ex persona; Alexander Severus); c. Praeterea (title not stated — perhaps X 2.19 De probationibus, chapter not identified); Code 2.4.2 (De transactionibus); and the law Sive possidetis (C. 4.19.16) cited above at {g}
notes.original: l. ex perſoſona. C. de proba. c. præterea l. ij de tranſactio. l. ſiue poſſideris. allegu.
notes.gloss: The print's perſoſona doubles a syllable of perſona; allegu. = alleguee, "already cited".
